full_text_en:
Peishi Investment Co., Ltd. v. Tianjin Metal Tools Company — Dispute over Sino-Foreign Joint Venture Contract (Appeal)

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2002) Min Si Zhong Zi No. 3

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Pearl Time Investments Limited. Address: 28th Floor, Bank of China Tower, No. 1 Garden Road, Central, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

Legal Representative: Zhang Sai'e, Director of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Wu Xudong, Attorney at Beijing Mingren Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Hao Baoping, Attorney at Beijing Mingren Law Firm.

Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance): Tianjin Metal Tools Company. Address: No. 10, Liuxinli, Enxinghou Street, Dagu South Road, Hexi District, Tianjin.

Legal Representative: Xu Lianqi, Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Hu Xueyun, Head of the Marketing Department of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Tao, Attorney at Tianjin Yifa Law Firm.

Appellant Pearl Time Investments Limited (hereinafter referred to as the Investment Company), in a dispute with Respondent Tianjin Metal Tools Company (hereinafter referred to as the Tools Company) over a Sino-foreign joint venture contract, appealed against the civil judgment (2000) Gao Jing Chu Zi No. 42 rendered by the Tianjin High People's Court to this Court. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law, with Presiding Judge Yu Lingyu, Judge Wang Yun, and Acting Judge Gao Xiaoli as members, and held a public hearing. The Appellant's agents ad litem Wu Xudong and Hao Baoping, and the Respondent's agents ad litem Hu Xueyun and Zhang Tao appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. The case has now been concluded.

The court at first instance found the following facts upon trial:

On January 12, 1994, the Investment Company and the Tools Company entered into a contract for the joint operation of Tianjin Nanhua Tools (Group) Co., Ltd. (the joint venture). The contract provided: the total investment in the joint venture was RMB 25,180,000, and the registered capital was RMB 150,912,000; the contribution ratio was 51% for the Investment Company, i.e., RMB 76,965,000, and 49% for the Tools Company, i.e., RMB 73,947,000; the Investment Company was to contribute cash in five installments, with 25% to be paid within the first month after obtaining the business license, 15% within the sixth month, 15% within the twelfth month, 20% within the eighteenth month, and the full registered capital within the twenty-fourth month; the Tools Company was to contribute its existing fixed assets, branch factories, sales offices, and other tertiary industry assets at valuation, including 68,708.79 square meters of buildings valued at RMB 26,109,400 and 2,102 units of equipment valued at RMB 47,837,600, to be paid in full in a lump sum within one month after obtaining the business license; both parties were to pay their respective capital contributions in full within the time limits stipulated in the contract, and any party that delayed in making payment was to pay delayed interest at a monthly rate of 2% of the outstanding amount, and the matter was to be handled in accordance with the "Interim Provisions of Tianjin Municipality on the Payment of Registered Capital Within the Prescribed Time Limit by Foreign-Invested Enterprises"; the term of the joint venture was 50 years, commencing from the date of issuance of the joint venture's business license; the joint venture was to adopt a system of responsibility of the general manager under the leadership of the board of directors, with the chairman of the board appointed by the Investment Company and the general manager recommended by the Tools Company. The contract also provided that if a party failed to perform its obligations under the contract or the articles of association, or seriously violated the provisions of the contract or articles of association, thereby rendering the joint venture unable to operate or unable to achieve the business objectives stipulated in the contract, that party was deemed to have unilaterally terminated the contract, and the other party had the right not only to claim compensation from the breaching party but also to report to the original approving authority for approval to terminate the contract. If either party was unable to perform, it was to promptly notify the other party and bear responsibility for its actions and the resulting consequences.

On January 19, 1994, the Tianjin Municipal People's Government issued the "Certificate of Approval" for the joint venture. On February 7 of the same year, the joint venture obtained the "Business License for Enterprise Legal Person." On February 27, 1994, Tianjin Xietong Certified Public Accountants issued a report on the capital contributions to the joint venture, confirming that both parties had contributed registered capital of RMB 92,947,000 as agreed, of which the Investment Company had contributed cash of USD 2,211,622, representing 25% of its required registered capital. On January 3 and April 5, 1995, the said accounting firm issued two further reports, confirming that the Investment Company had made its second and third capital contributions as agreed, but that RMB 34,635,840.67 was still outstanding. The Tools Company had contributed buildings and equipment equivalent to RMB 73,947,000, representing 100% of its required registered capital.

On March 6, 1996, the Tools Company sent a letter titled "Regarding the Late Payment of the Fourth and Fifth Installments of Registered Capital by the Hong Kong Party" to the Tianjin Hebei District Administration for Industry and Commerce, demanding that the Investment Company make timely payment of its capital, failing which it would bear the losses caused by the late payment, and requesting the industrial and commercial authorities to assist in urging the payment of the fourth and fifth installments of registered capital. On March 15, 1996, the Hebei District Administration for Industry and Commerce issued a notice to the joint venture demanding payment of the registered capital within one month from receipt of the notice, failing which action would be taken. On March 27, 1998, the Tools Company sent a letter to the Investment Company, urging that all capital should be fully paid, failing which the Investment Company would bear all consequences. However, the Investment Company never paid the capital required under the joint venture contract thereafter.

The fixed assets contributed by the Tools Company had been used by the joint venture since its establishment. However, some buildings were not registered for transfer of title. The investment value of the buildings not registered for title transfer was RMB 5,303,000.

After the establishment of the joint venture, from 1995 to 1999, Tianjin Binhai Certified Public Accountants was responsible for the annual audit of the joint venture.

The court at first instance also found: On June 24, 1998, the Tools Company filed a lawsuit in the Tianjin No. 2 Intermediate People's Court, seeking an order for the Investment Company to pay delayed interest on the unpaid fourth installment. The Tianjin No. 2 Intermediate People's Court, in its civil judgment (1998) Er Zhong Jing Yi Chu Zi No. 167, ordered the Investment Company to pay to the Tools Company delayed interest on the fourth installment of RMB 15,393,000. The Investment Company appealed that judgment. The Tianjin High People's Court, in its civil judgment (1999) Gao Jing Zhong Zi No. 100, dismissed the appeal and upheld the original judgment. Based on that effective judgment, the Tianjin No. 2 Intermediate People's Court commissioned Tianjin Licheng Certified Public Accountants to audit the assets of the joint venture and ruled that the net equity of RMB 15,785,478.54 owned by the Investment Company in the joint venture be transferred to the Tools Company as compensation. The Tianjin Municipal Commission of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation, in its document Jin Jing Mao Zi Guan [2001] No. 16, agreed in principle to change the nature of the joint venture from a Sino-foreign equity joint venture to a domestic enterprise.

The parties had no objection to the above facts found by the court at first instance during the second instance, and this Court confirms them.

The Tools Company alleged in its complaint: According to the joint venture contract, the Investment Company was to contribute cash in five installments totaling RMB 76,965,000, representing 51% of the registered capital. However, it only contributed three installments totaling RMB 42,330,000. The fourth and fifth installments of RMB 34,634,000 remained unpaid, in violation of the contract and articles of association, not only infringing upon the legitimate rights and interests of the Tools Company but also causing losses to the joint venture. Therefore, it filed a lawsuit with the Tianjin High People's Court, requesting an order that the Investment Company pay delayed interest of RMB 13,469,000 on the fifth unpaid installment of RMB 19,240,000 (as of the end of 1998) in accordance with the joint venture contract, and that the contract for Tianjin Nanhua Tools (Group) Co., Ltd. be terminated.

The court at first instance held: The joint venture contract signed by the parties, both in its execution and content, did not violate legal provisions and should be confirmed as valid. According to the provisions of the joint venture contract, the Investment Company was to contribute capital in cash in five installments. The Investment Company only made the first three installments as stipulated and failed to make the fourth and fifth installments, which clearly constituted a breach of contract. The Tools Company contributed its existing fixed assets, branch factories, sales offices, and other tertiary industry assets at valuation, to be paid in full in a lump sum within one month after obtaining the business license. The assets contributed by the Tools Company had been delivered to the joint venture for actual use as agreed, and upon confirmation by the joint venture's chairman of the board, Wu Hongsheng, appointed by the Investment Company, and the deputy chairman Xu Lianqi, appointed by the Tools Company, an application was made to the administrative department for industry and commerce for change of registration, and title registration for the vast majority of the fixed assets was completed. Although the Tools Company had not completed the title transfer procedures for some fixed assets after they were actually put into use, this did not affect the normal operation of the joint venture. However, the Investment Company's insufficient capital investment directly affected the joint venture's operations and expected benefits, leading to losses. For this, the Investment Company should bear liability for breach of contract. Since the Investment Company did not raise any objection before the lawsuit regarding the incomplete title registration of some of the Tools Company's fixed assets, and according to the relevant letters issued by the Investment Company, the reasons for its failure to invest as agreed were "the company's business situation was very unsatisfactory and was suffering losses" and "hoping for policy assistance and support from the government," the Tools Company's failure to complete the title transfer procedures for some fixed assets was not the reason for the Investment Company's failure to continue its capital contributions.

The joint venture adopted a system of responsibility of the general manager under the leadership of the board of directors. Based on the relevant evidence provided by both parties, the board of directors, as the highest authority of the joint venture, had been exercising its functions, and the Investment Company, as the controlling shareholder, had decision-making power until the dispute arose, when the board of directors dismissed the general manager appointed by the Tools Company. In the daily management of the joint venture, the Investment Company stationed directors, deputy general managers, and financial personnel in the joint venture, received periodic financial reports, and participated in the management of the joint venture. Therefore, the Investment Company's argument that "due to the plaintiff's interference, the defendant was unable to participate in the joint venture's operations, and due to the plaintiff's poor management, the joint venture had been in a state of loss" had no factual basis and was not supported.

Since the selection of the accounting firm that conducted the annual audit of the joint venture was recognized by the Investment Company, and the Investment Company did not raise any objection to the audit reports over the years before the dispute arose, the audit reports remain valid. Therefore, the Investment Company's request for a new audit had no legal basis.

The Investment Company had no valid reason or basis to breach the joint venture contract by failing to continue its investment. It should have made the required capital contributions and assumed liability for breach of contract. However, since both parties in this litigation requested the termination of the joint venture contract, such a request should be supported. Therefore, the capital contributions stipulated in the joint venture contract would no longer be made. The Tools Company's claim for delayed interest on the unpaid fifth installment should be supported. The court at first instance, in accordance with Article 7 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Articles 84 and 85 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, ruled: 1. The joint venture contract for Tianjin Nanhua Tools (Group) Co., Ltd. was terminated; 2. Pearl Time Investments Limited was to pay to Tianjin Metal Tools Company delayed interest on the unpaid fifth installment of RMB 19,240,000 (calculated at a monthly rate of 2% from February 8, 1996, to the date this judgment takes effect).

The Investment Company, dissatisfied with the original judgment, appealed, stating: 1. The original judgment seriously violated statutory procedures, leading to an incorrect decision. The Tianjin High People's Court did not present or have the parties cross-examine the accounting archives of the joint venture that it had preserved through evidence preservation, especially the original vouchers and accounting vouchers in the accounting archives, which seriously violated the relevant provisions of China's substantive and procedural laws. 2. The original judgment had unclear facts and insufficient evidence. It found that the Tools Company had completed title registration procedures for the vast majority of its fixed assets, but in fact, the equipment worth RMB 47,837,600, as part of the false joint venture, had never been transferred through title procedures in the administrative department for industry and commerce, violating Articles 8 and 24 of the "Provisional Regulations on the Administration of Company Registered Capital" published by the State Administration for Industry and Commerce in 1995; the 18 branch factories of the Tools Company had not been registered with the industry and commerce authorities after the joint venture; Xu Lianqi, the general manager of the Tools Company, had simultaneously served as the general manager and director of the joint venture for seven years from the date the joint venture obtained its business license, violating Article 40, paragraph 4 of the "Implementing Regulations for the Law on Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Ventures" and Article 61 of the "Company Law of the People's Republic of China"; the financial institution of the joint venture used the financial institution of the Tools Company, and the various original vouchers and financial books of the joint venture were kept strictly confidential from the Investment Company, depriving the Investment Company of its management rights in the joint venture. 3. The original judgment applied the law incorrectly. At the time of the first instance trial, the Contract Law had already been implemented. Articles 68 and 69 of that law established the system of the right to suspend performance for insecurity, and Articles 108 and 94, paragraph 2, established the system of anticipatory breach. After the Investment Company paid the first three installments, it was still excluded from the joint venture. The Tools Company's actions indicated that it would not perform its obligations under the joint venture contract. In such circumstances, the Investment Company's cessation of further investment was an exercise of the right to suspend performance for insecurity and did not constitute a breach. The law requires that the capital contributions of the joint venture parties to the joint venture are formal legal acts, yet the original judgment held that non-monetary contributions need not go through title transfer procedures as long as they were actually used by the joint venture, openly contradicting legal provisions. Therefore, the Investment Company requested that the court of second instance ascertain the facts and amend the judgment according to law.

The Tools Company argued in its defense: The Investment Company's claims of "right to suspend performance for insecurity" and "anticipatory breach" lacked factual and legal basis. The Tools Company's capital contributions had been fully paid as agreed. The fixed assets contributed had been actually used by the joint venture since its opening. The Investment Company had hired auditors from Hong Kong and conducted multiple audits of the joint venture, but never raised any objection to the Tools Company's capital contributions before filing the lawsuit, nor did it fulfill the obligation to give notice or assert any claim regarding the Tools Company's capital contributions. Moreover, there was no prior breach by the Tools Company, because the joint venture contract stipulated that the Tools Company's capital contributions were to be paid in full within one month after obtaining the business license, and it did not require that title transfer procedures for fixed assets be completed within one month. The failure to promptly transfer title for a few factory buildings did not affect the joint venture's production and operation. The appointment of senior management of the joint venture was made by the board of directors, the establishment of the joint venture's management structure was decided by the board, the authorization of the joint venture's general manager and branch managers was also unanimously agreed by the board, and the joint venture reported its business situation to the board and was subject to its supervision. Moreover, the audit institution selected by both parties audited the joint venture annually. Therefore, the Investment Company's claim that the Tools Company excluded the Investment Company from the joint venture was contrary to objective facts. As for the Investment Company's argument that the joint venture's general manager simultaneously served as the general manager of the Tools Company, violating relevant state laws, that was a common-sense error. Serving concurrently as the manager of such a company was merely to fulfill shareholder duties, did not cause losses to the joint venture, and did not fall within the circumstances of "prohibition of competing business." Therefore, the facts found in the original judgment were correct, and the Investment Company's grounds for appeal lacked factual and legal basis, and should be dismissed.

This Court holds that this case is a dispute over a Sino-foreign equity joint venture contract. Pursuant to Article 246 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, it shall be under the jurisdiction of the People's Court of the People's Republic of China. The Tianjin High People's Court, as the court of the place of performance of the Sino-foreign equity joint venture contract, has jurisdiction over this case. Pursuant to Article 5, paragraph 2 of the Law of the People's Republic of China on Foreign-Related Economic Contracts, which was effective at the time, contracts for Sino-foreign equity joint ventures performed within the territory of the People's Republic of China shall be governed by the law of the People's Republic of China. Therefore, the law of the People's Republic of China applies to this case.

The contract for the joint operation of Tianjin Nanhua Tools (Group) Co., Ltd. signed by the Investment Company and the Tools Company was voluntarily negotiated and concluded by the parties. Its contents did not violate legal provisions and, having been submitted to and approved by the local people's government as required, are valid. Neither party disputed the validity of the joint venture contract during the first and second instances.

According to the provisions of the joint venture contract, the Investment Company's contribution ratio was 51%, i.e., RMB 76,965,000, to be paid in cash in five installments. The first three installments totaling RMB 42,330,000 had been paid into the joint venture as agreed, as confirmed by three reports issued by Tianjin Xietong Certified Public Accountants. The remaining two installments totaling RMB 34,635,840.67 had not been paid. The Tools Company's contribution ratio was 49%, i.e., RMB 73,947,000, to be contributed in the form of its fixed assets, branch factories, sales offices, and other tertiary industry assets at valuation. The Tools Company had delivered the above equipment and buildings to the joint venture for actual use as agreed. Both parties had no dispute regarding the payment of the above registered capital.

The focal points of dispute between the parties in this case are: 1. Did the Investment Company's cessation of further capital contributions after paying the first three installments as agreed constitute a breach of contract and require it to bear liability? 2. Did the Tools Company deprive the Investment Company of its management rights in the joint venture?

Article 23 of the joint venture contract stipulates that one of the Investment Company's responsibilities and obligations is "to provide cash in accordance with Article 13 (regarding contribution ratio), Article 14 (regarding capital composition of contributions), and Article 16 (regarding liability for late payment) of Chapter 5 of this contract." The fourth installment accounted for 20% of the registered capital, and the contract required it to be paid within the eighteenth month after obtaining the business license. The fifth installment accounted for 25%, to be paid within the twenty-fourth month after obtaining the business license. From the facts found in this case, the reasons for the Investment Company's failure to pay the fourth and fifth installments as agreed were "the company's business situation was very unsatisfactory and was suffering losses" and "hoping for policy assistance and support from the government." This was confirmed by letters written by Zhang Sai'e, a director of the Investment Company, to relevant leaders and departments of Tianjin. The Investment Company did not dispute the authenticity of the contents of these letters during the second instance. The Tools Company, as a party to the joint venture, was required by the contract to contribute its existing fixed assets, branch factories, sales offices, and other tertiary industry assets at valuation, to be paid in full in a lump sum within one month after obtaining the business license. The assets contributed by the Tools Company had been delivered to the joint venture for actual use as agreed. According to Article 72 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, "ownership of property is transferred at the time of delivery of the property, unless otherwise provided by law." For equipment contributed as capital, delivery constitutes transfer; however, for buildings, title transfer is required by law as a condition for property rights transfer. The Tools Company's failure to complete title transfer procedures for a small number of buildings after they were actually put into use in the joint venture constituted a breach of contract, but it did not affect the normal operation of the joint venture, and the Investment Company did not raise any objection before the lawsuit was filed. Therefore, this was not the reason for the Investment Company's failure to pay the fourth and fifth installments as agreed.

As the Foreign Economic Contract Law of the PRC, which was effective at that time, did not contain provisions on the defense of insecurity or anticipatory breach. Article 1 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation (I) on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "For disputes arising from contracts concluded before the implementation of the Contract Law that are brought to the People's Court, unless otherwise provided in this Interpretation, the legal provisions in effect at that time shall apply; where there are no applicable legal provisions at that time, the relevant provisions of the Contract Law may apply." Accordingly, the relevant provisions of the PRC Contract Law concerning the defense of insecurity and anticipatory breach may be applied to this case. Pursuant to Articles 68 and 69 of the Contract Law regarding the defense of insecurity, a party who is obligated to perform first must have concrete evidence to prove that the other party is in one of the statutorily prescribed circumstances demonstrating that it has lost or may lose the ability to perform its obligations, and must also fulfill the obligation to notify the other party in a timely manner. In this case, there was no issue of which party between the Investment Company and the Tool Company should perform first, and the Investment Company did not notify the Tool Company of its intention to suspend performance of the joint venture contract. Therefore, the requirements for the defense of insecurity under the Contract Law are not met. Furthermore, the Tool Company had already delivered the equipment and real property contributed as capital to the joint venture company for actual use, with only a small portion of real property not yet having undergone the transfer of title registration. The Tool Company performed its principal obligations, rather than failing to perform its principal obligations, so this also does not meet the requirements for anticipatory breach under Article 94 of the Contract Law. Consequently, the Investment Company's ground of appeal that its failure to contribute the fourth and fifth tranches of capital as agreed constituted an anticipatory breach entitling it to exercise the defense of insecurity, and thus it could be exempted from liability, cannot be established. This Court does not support it.

Article 31 of the joint venture contract provides that the joint venture company shall adopt a system of general manager responsibility under the leadership of the board of directors. According to the minutes of the board of directors of the joint venture company provided by both parties, the board of directors was established at the commencement of the company's operations. The board of directors consisted of nine directors, with four appointed by the Tool Company and five appointed by the Investment Company. The chairman of the board was appointed by the Investment Company, and the vice-chairman was appointed by the Tool Company. The board of directors performed its normal functions, including appointing Xu Lianqi as the general manager of the joint venture company, discussing and approving the company's accounting system, and deciding on the company's business policies and decisions. Article 33 of the joint venture contract provides: "Unless approved by the board of directors, the general manager and deputy general manager shall not concurrently serve as the general manager or deputy general manager of any other economic organization, nor shall they participate in commercial competition against the joint venture company on behalf of any other economic organization." In this case, Xu Lianqi was appointed by the Tool Company to serve as the general manager of the joint venture company. The minutes of the first board of directors meeting recorded that the board of directors appointed Xu Lianqi as the general manager of the joint venture company. The Tool Company had invested its entire business operations in the joint venture with the Investment Company. Pursuant to Reply Letter No. 60 (Qi Wai Zi [1987]) of the Registration Department of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce: "Given that after a Chinese-invested enterprise makes a full-investment contribution to a Sino-foreign equity joint venture, the Chinese-invested enterprise still needs to perform the contract and articles of association, share profits, and bear risks as an independent legal person, it shall therefore retain its status as an independent legal person." The PRC Company Law and the Implementation Regulations of the Law of the PRC on Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Ventures provide that the general manager or deputy general manager shall not concurrently serve as the general manager or deputy general manager of any other economic organization, nor shall they participate in commercial competition against the enterprise on behalf of any other economic organization. The term "other economic organization" as used here obviously does not include the Chinese-invested enterprise that has made a full-investment contribution to a Sino-foreign equity joint venture. Merely retaining the independent legal person status of the Chinese-invested enterprise cannot create competition with the joint venture company. The Investment Company also failed to provide evidence proving that the Tool Company participated in competition. Moreover, under the system of general manager responsibility under the leadership of the board of directors, matters such as the type of financial institution used by the joint venture company and how to supervise and manage its finances are internal management issues of the joint venture company and are unrelated to the actions of the shareholders. Even if the Investment Company believed that a particular management action of the joint venture company infringed upon its lawful rights and interests, it could only assert its claims against the joint venture company, not against one of its shareholders. Therefore, the appellant, the Investment Company's grounds of appeal, including that the general manager of the joint venture company had long concurrently served as the legal representative of the Tool Company in violation of state laws, that the joint venture company used the same financial institution as the Tool Company, and that the Tool Company had deprived the Investment Company of its management and operational rights over the joint venture company, lack factual and legal basis. This Court does not support them.

The appellant, the Investment Company, argued both at first instance and on appeal that the annual audit reports issued by Tianjin Binhai Accounting Firm were invalid and requested a new audit, on the grounds that the audit reports did not and could not verify the original vouchers, accounting vouchers, etc., and that precisely these original vouchers and accounting vouchers were unreliable, thus making it impossible to confirm the authenticity of the audit reports. In this case, Tianjin Binhai Accounting Firm was recommended by the Investment Company as the auditor. The other two joint venture companies established by the Investment Company in Tianjin, Tianjin Jingang (Group) Co., Ltd. and Nanhua Group (Tianjin) Garment Co., Ltd., also commissioned Binhai Accounting Firm to conduct audit and accounting consulting services. The Investment Company had no objections to the annual audit reports for 1995 to 1999 issued by the firm prior to the litigation. Since the Investment Company did not provide contrary evidence to challenge the validity of the said audit reports, the court of first instance's refusal to grant its application for a new audit was not improper.

During the first instance proceedings, the Tianjin High People's Court, upon the application of the Investment Company, preserved the evidence of the original financial vouchers and accounting vouchers of the joint venture company. The appellant, the Investment Company, requested both at first instance and on appeal that the preserved evidentiary materials be subject to court examination, arguing that only through such examination could the true use and destination of the Investment Company's first three tranches of cash capital contributions totaling RMB 42.33 million be ascertained, and the true cause of the joint venture company's losses be identified. This case involves a dispute over a Sino-foreign equity joint venture contract, and the ultimate issue is whether one or both parties violated the provisions of the joint venture contract. Issues such as the true use and destination of the first three tranches of cash capital contributions totaling RMB 42.33 million by one joint venture party, or whether the joint venture company suffered losses, the causes of such losses, and the amount of losses, are not issues to be resolved in this case. According to law, these issues should be resolved after the termination of the joint venture contract through the formation of a liquidation committee, which will conduct a comprehensive inventory of the joint venture's assets, claims, and debts. In this case, although the court of first instance took evidence preservation measures for the original financial vouchers and accounting vouchers of the joint venture company, these materials were not admitted as evidence for the determination of facts in this case. Therefore, it was not improper for the court of first instance to refrain from conducting a court examination of the preserved evidence materials.

The joint venture contract is valid and should, in principle, be performed. However, both parties in the litigation have requested the termination of the joint venture contract. This request should be granted. The court of first instance correctly decided that the parties should no longer continue to perform the joint venture contract.

In summary, this Court holds that the facts found in the first instance judgment are clear and the application of law is correct. Pursuant to Article 153, paragraph 1, item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

The appeal is dismissed and the original judgment is affirmed.

The court costs for the first instance shall be borne according to the first instance judgment. The court costs for the second instance, amounting to RMB 75,410, shall be borne by the appellant, Pace Investment Co., Ltd.

This judgment is the final judgment.

Presiding Judge: Yu Lingyu
Judge: Wang Yun
Acting Judge: Gao Xiaoli
June 20, 2003
Clerk: Yang Honglei
